questions.prompt: Biotechnology is based on microbiology. What does microbiology study?
options: The movement of the planets
Very small living things such as bacteria and fungi
The rocks and minerals in soil
The weather and the climate
questions.explanation: Microbiology is the study of micro-organisms, the tiny living things like bacteria and fungi that are usually too small to see.

questions.topic: Useful product in bread and injera
questions.prompt: In injera and bread making, which product of yeast is the one we actually want?
options: Ethanol, because it adds alcohol
Carbon dioxide, because it makes the dough rise
Lactic acid, because it adds sourness
Oxygen, because it feeds the dough
questions.explanation: In baking, the wanted product is the carbon dioxide gas, which is trapped in the dough and makes it rise. Ethanol is the wanted product in drinks.

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes are there in total in a normal human body cell?
questions.explanation: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes in total, arranged as 23 matching (homologous) pairs.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes what good health means?
options: Only being strong enough to lift heavy loads
Simply not being able to feel any pain
Full physical, mental and social well-being, not only the absence of disease
Having a large number of red blood cells
questions.explanation: Health is a state of full physical, mental and social well-being. It is more than just being free of illness.

questions.prompt: Inside a leaf cell, in which structure does photosynthesis take place?
options: The chloroplast
The cell wall
The vacuole
The nucleus
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis happens in the chloroplasts, the structures that contain the green pigment chlorophyll.

questions.prompt: The word biodiversity means the:
options: Amount of coal under the ground
Variety of different living species in an area
Speed of the river flowing through a valley
Number of factories in a region
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of different living species (plants, animals and others) found in an area.

questions.prompt: Compared with aerobic respiration, how much energy does the anaerobic respiration of yeast release from the same amount of sugar?
options: Much more energy
Exactly the same amount
Only a little energy
No energy at all
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration (fermentation) releases only a little energy because the sugar is not fully broken down. Aerobic respiration releases much more.

questions.prompt: A piece of DNA has 30 adenine (A) bases. Using the pairing rules, how many thymine (T) bases must it have?
options: It cannot be known
questions.explanation: Adenine always pairs with thymine, so for every A there is one T. With 30 adenine bases there must be 30 thymine bases.

questions.prompt: In which organs of the body does meiosis take place?
options: In the skin and the lungs
In the reproductive organs (ovaries and testes)
In the stomach and the liver
In every cell of the body all the time
questions.explanation: Meiosis makes sex cells (sperm and eggs), so it happens in the reproductive organs: the testes and the ovaries.

questions.prompt: How do the skeletal and muscular systems work together to move the body?
options: Muscles pull on bones to make the body move
Bones squeeze blood through the muscles
Muscles digest the food inside the bones
Bones make oxygen for the muscles
questions.explanation: Bones support the body and muscles are attached to them. When a muscle contracts, it pulls on a bone, causing movement.

questions.prompt: Where does the carbon dioxide used in photosynthesis come from?
options: It is taken up from the soil by the roots
It diffuses into the leaf from the air through the stomata
It is made by the chlorophyll from water
It is carried up the xylem from the roots
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide diffuses into the leaf from the surrounding air through the stomata. Water, by contrast, comes up from the roots.

questions.prompt: Malaria is a communicable disease. How does it pass from one person to another?
options: Through the bite of an infected mosquito
By breathing the same air in a room
By eating sugary food
By touching a healthy person's hand
questions.explanation: Malaria is spread by the bite of an infected mosquito, which is why bed nets and removing standing water help prevent it.

questions.prompt: Water is called a renewable resource. What condition must be met for it to stay available?
options: It must be used much faster than it is replaced
It must be used and managed carefully so it is not wasted or polluted
It must never be used by anyone
It must be turned into coal first
questions.explanation: A renewable resource only lasts if it is used wisely. Water must be protected from waste and pollution so it can keep being replaced naturally.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the cells made by mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis makes 2 identical cells; meiosis makes 4 different cells
Mitosis makes 4 different cells; meiosis makes 2 identical cells
Both make 2 identical cells
Both make 4 different cells
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces 2 cells identical to the parent, while meiosis produces 4 cells that differ and have half the chromosome number.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the circulatory system?
options: To break food into small molecules
To transport oxygen, glucose and wastes around the body in the blood
To take air into the body
To control the body with nerves
questions.explanation: The circulatory system, with the heart and blood vessels, transports oxygen, glucose and waste substances around the body in the blood.

questions.prompt: Bubbles given off by a pondweed in bright light are collected and a glowing splint placed in the gas relights. Which gas was collected?
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Hydrogen
questions.explanation: A glowing splint relighting is the test for oxygen. Photosynthesis releases oxygen, so the bubbles from the pondweed are oxygen.

questions.prompt: How does letting too many animals graze the same land lead to soil erosion?
options: The animals add fertile topsoil to the land
The animals strip the plants away, leaving bare soil that is easily washed or blown off
The animals press the soil into solid rock
The animals make the grass roots grow deeper
questions.explanation: Overgrazing removes the plant cover and roots that hold the soil. The bare ground that is left is easily eroded by rain and wind.

questions.prompt: A student is told a food was made using a fungus, not bacteria. Which traditional product was most likely made?
options: Irgo (yoghurt)
Ayib (cheese)
Tella (a fermented drink)
Sour milk
questions.explanation: Tella is fermented by yeast, which is a fungus. Irgo, ayib and sour milk are all made by bacteria carrying out lactic fermentation.

questions.prompt: One DNA strand reads T-A-C-G-G. What is the base sequence of the strand paired with it?
options: T-A-C-G-G
A-T-G-C-C
G-G-C-A-T
C-C-G-T-A
questions.explanation: Using A-T and C-G pairing, T-A-C-G-G pairs with A-T-G-C-C, base by base.

questions.prompt: A dividing cell copies its chromosomes and then divides only once to give two cells with the same chromosome number as the parent. Which process is this?
options: Meiosis, making sex cells
Mitosis, used for growth and repair
Fermentation, releasing energy
Fertilisation, joining two cells
questions.explanation: Copying chromosomes then dividing once to give two cells with the full chromosome number is mitosis, which is used for growth and repair.

questions.prompt: Why must the digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems all work together for a leg muscle to keep contracting?
options: The digestive system supplies glucose, the respiratory system supplies oxygen, and the circulatory system delivers both to the muscle
Each system makes the muscle on its own without help
Only the circulatory system is involved in muscle contraction
The three systems compete and slow the muscle down
questions.explanation: Muscle respiration needs glucose from the digestive system and oxygen from the respiratory system, both delivered by the blood of the circulatory system. No system works alone.

questions.prompt: An animal has 24 chromosomes in its body cells. How many chromosomes will be in each of its sex cells after meiosis?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so a body cell with 24 chromosomes produces sex cells with 12 chromosomes each.

questions.prompt: Before testing a leaf to prove light is needed for photosynthesis, the plant is first kept in the dark for two days. Why is this step important?
options: To make the leaf greener
To use up any stored starch, so new starch can only come from fresh photosynthesis
To add extra carbon dioxide to the leaf
To kill the cells before the test
questions.explanation: Keeping the plant in the dark first removes any starch already stored. Then any starch found after the test must have been made during the experiment.

questions.prompt: A student says 'breathing and respiration are the same thing.' Why is this statement wrong?
options: Breathing is moving air in and out, but respiration is the release of energy from glucose inside cells
Breathing only happens in plants and respiration only in animals
Respiration moves air and breathing makes energy
They are different words for moving blood around
questions.explanation: Breathing is the physical movement of air into and out of the lungs. Respiration is the chemical reaction inside cells that releases energy from glucose. They are not the same.

questions.prompt: A doctor sees four patients: one with tuberculosis, one with cholera, one with malaria and one with diabetes. Which patient has a disease that cannot spread to other people?
options: The patient with tuberculosis
The patient with cholera
The patient with malaria
The patient with diabetes
questions.explanation: Diabetes is non-communicable and cannot pass to others. Tuberculosis, cholera and malaria are all communicable diseases that can spread between people or via a vector.

questions.prompt: On a warm, sunny day with plenty of carbon dioxide, a plant in dry soil still grows slowly. Which factor is most likely limiting its photosynthesis?
options: Water, because the soil is dry
Light, because the day is sunny
Carbon dioxide, although it is plentiful
Temperature, although it is warm
questions.explanation: Light, carbon dioxide and warmth are all plentiful, so the only raw material in short supply is water. The dry soil makes water the limiting factor.

questions.prompt: When injera batter is cooked on the hot mitad, the many small holes (eyes) appear because the:
options: Trapped carbon dioxide bubbles expand in the heat
Ethanol turns into solid starch
Bacteria suddenly multiply in the heat
Water turns into chlorophyll
questions.explanation: During fermentation yeast makes carbon dioxide that is trapped in the batter. On heating, these gas bubbles expand, leaving the holes that make injera spongy.

questions.prompt: Two children of the same parents look different from each other, yet a cut on the skin heals with identical new cells. Which pair of processes explains this?
options: Meiosis makes varied sex cells; mitosis makes identical cells for repair
Mitosis makes varied cells; meiosis makes identical cells for repair
Both differences come only from mitosis
Both come only from fermentation
questions.explanation: Meiosis shuffles the parents' genes so each sex cell is different, giving varied children. Mitosis makes exact copies, so a wound heals with identical cells.

questions.prompt: After a forested hillside is cleared, fertile topsoil is quickly washed downhill in the rains. What is the main reason removing the trees caused this?
options: Tree roots and cover that held the soil and slowed the rain were removed
The trees used to push the soil downhill themselves
Cutting trees adds extra topsoil that washes away
Trees normally make the rain fall harder
questions.explanation: Tree roots grip the soil and the leaf cover slows the rain. Once the trees are gone, bare loose soil is washed straight downhill, causing erosion.

questions.prompt: The same yeast cell can give different products. Which row correctly matches the conditions to the products?
options: With oxygen: ethanol + carbon dioxide; without oxygen: carbon dioxide + water
With oxygen: carbon dioxide + water; without oxygen: ethanol + carbon dioxide
With oxygen: lactic acid; without oxygen: oxygen
With oxygen: ethanol only; without oxygen: water only
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration (with oxygen) gives carbon dioxide and water. Anaerobic respiration (without oxygen), called fermentation, gives ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: A hospital needs a steady supply of insulin that exactly matches human insulin and is pure and plentiful. Which approach should it choose, and why?
options: Selective breeding of cattle, because it is the fastest method
Genetic engineering of bacteria, because they make exact human insulin in large pure amounts
Fermenting teff with wild yeast, because it makes hormones cheaply
Collecting insulin from wild animals, because it needs no laboratory
questions.explanation: Inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria makes them produce exact human insulin reliably, purely and in large amounts, which the other methods cannot do.

questions.prompt: A school has outbreaks of both cholera (from dirty water) and malaria (from mosquitoes). Which combined plan tackles both diseases at their source?
options: Provide clean, treated drinking water and clear standing water while using bed nets
Ask everyone to eat less salt and rest more
Vaccinate all pupils against diabetes
Cut down nearby trees and stop washing hands
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads through dirty water and malaria through mosquitoes that breed in standing water. Clean water plus removing standing water and using bed nets attacks both at the source.

questions.prompt: A couple has two sons and wants to know the chance their third child will be a daughter. What is the best answer?
options: Zero, because they only have sons
About 1 in 2, because the father can pass X or Y with equal chance
About 1 in 4, because two sons were already born
Certain to be a daughter, to balance the family
questions.explanation: Each child is independent of the others. The father's sperm carries X (daughter) or Y (son) with equal chance, so each child has about a 50% chance of being a daughter.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to test whether adding carbon dioxide raises the rate of photosynthesis in a greenhouse. To make a fair test, the farmer should:
options: Change the carbon dioxide level while keeping light and temperature the same
Change the carbon dioxide, the light and the temperature all at once
Use a different type of plant in each greenhouse
Keep everything, including the carbon dioxide, exactly the same
questions.explanation: In a fair test only one factor is changed at a time. Here only the carbon dioxide should change, while light, temperature and plant type are kept the same.

questions.prompt: A rural village relies on firewood and the surrounding forest is shrinking fast. Switching to a biogas digester fed by animal dung would help conservation BEST because it:
options: Uses up the village's drinking water supply
Reduces the need to cut trees, helping the forest and the soil and wildlife it supports
Releases far more carbon dioxide than any other fuel
Removes all the bacteria from the soil
questions.explanation: A biogas digester makes methane from waste, so the village burns less firewood. Fewer trees are cut, which protects the forest and the soil and wildlife depending on it.

questions.prompt: A farming community on a steep, eroding slope wants to keep farming while saving their soil. Which plan is best?
options: Plough up and down the slope so water drains off faster
Build terraces and plant trees, then grow crops on the level steps
Remove all plants so the crops have no competition
Let cattle graze the bare slope freely all year
questions.explanation: Terraces slow water running downhill and tree roots hold the soil, so crops can be grown on the level steps while erosion is reduced. The other choices would worsen erosion.
